newsitem.title: USA: One black on grand jury for St. Petersburg shooting.
newsitem.headline: One black on grand jury for St. Petersburg shooting.

text.p: Just one black will be in a grand jury on the shooting of a black motorist by a white police officer that sparked riots last week in this Florida city, the state attorney said Wednesday.
The jury will meet next Wednesday to decide whether to indict officer James Knight, who shot dead 18-year-old Tyron Lewis last Thursday after stopping him for speeding.
"They will be dealing with the shooting incident -- if it was justifiable homicide," Pinellas County state attorney Bernie McCabe told Reuters.

Although the case is fraught with racial tensions, McCabe said only one black was on the 18-person jury. Asked if the others were all white or there were some of Asian extraction he said: "I don't know. It is picked randomly from the voters' rolls."
The standing jury was chosen before the shooting and the riots, he said. Leaders of the black community could not immediately be reached for comment.
Knight shot Lewis at the wheel of his car after stopping him. Police say Lewis appeared to move the car forward in an effort to run Knight and his colleague down.
Rioting then broke out in the poor black neighbourhood of South St.Petersburg. At least 11 people were hurt, mostly police officers, and nearly 30 fires set in shops, businesses and homes.
Police regained control in the early hours of Friday but the city was under a state of emergency, with National Guard units on standby, until Sunday night.
Black youths complain they are constantly victimised by police. Community leaders say poverty, lack of jobs and bleak prospects for blacks create resentment fuelling unrest.

A team from the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights went to St.Petersburg Wednesday to assess race relations after the trouble. The FBI has also announced it will launch an investigation of police conduct in the killing of Lewis.
